headline: Bega Cheese CEO highlights strong FY25 earnings growth driven by cost discipline, branded categories, and protein trends
reasoning: Bega delivered 12% normalised EBITDA growth to $225.6m and 36% normalised NPAT growth, underpinned by factory consolidation, modernisation, and investment in branded categories aligned with consumer wellness trends. The company's five number-one or number-two mainstream brands are supported by an 'operational moat' of best-in-class cost structures. Growth is coming from yogurt, milk-based beverages, cream cheese internationally, and higher-protein bulk and nutritionals exports. Management guided FY27 normalised EBITDA of $200-245m and sees continued solid momentum.
quote: Oh look, it's been a couple of years of hard work, Juliet. So we've, um, we've obviously been working very hard at our cost base over the last couple of years, and a lot of that's starting to bear fruit with factory consolidation and then modernising our existing factories. But but we're really pleased that we're also getting at the same time as doing that. We're also getting terrific top line growth. And so that's come through a focus on specific branded categories where we're we've innovated a lot of our product on on that's in line with consumer wellness trends. And we're getting good uptake there, particularly across yogurt milk based beverages. And then our our international businesses are doing very well around cream cheese product. And and and our bulk and nutritionals business has been able to really sort of, um, optimize the potential of opportunities around higher protein, um, you know, value add to a lot of our, a lot of our proteins that we ship overseas.
episode_title: Bega cuts the fat, builds the muscle
